A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LD3, with readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Their shared content can be matched despite substantial reorganization. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation experiments, FID measurements, component ablations, training-efficiency measurements, and empirical investigation of the theoretical bound.

after.justification: v2 retains original LD3 experiments and adds quantitative text-to-image evaluations, unconditional ImageNet-64 results, solver-transfer tests, and training-prompt sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: The hard and soft teacher-forcing objectives, LPIPS loss, constrained initial-noise optimization, monotonic time parameterization, decoupled network times, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. Describing the objective as global truncation-error optimization does not introduce a different algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix C.2 adds unconditional ImageNet-64 generation alongside the retained class-conditional ImageNet-256 task. The other image domains and text-to-image task were already represented. Adding InstaFlow and pixel-space LSUN models primarily expands model configurations within existing task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated DMN and GITS comparisons across retained benchmarks, GGDM+PRED+TIME in Table 11, and Progressive Distillation, Consistency Distillation, and Rectified Flow in Table 9. Several comparisons use externally reported scores rather than rerun baselines. The CIFAR10/FFHQ AYS comparison remains, but the earlier ImageNet-256 AYS entry disappears.

E3.justification: Appendix B.1.3 changes Stable Diffusion v1.4/Uni_PC with a 10-NFE uniform teacher to v1.5/iPNDM with a GITS teacher at student NFE plus one. v2 introduces 30K-caption Stable Diffusion and 10K-caption InstaFlow evaluations, DDIM/iDDPM configurations, and RMSD against 100-step DDIM. Latent-space tables also change solver-order labels from 2M to 3M; actual reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v2 adds solver-transfer analysis testing whether learned schedules generalize between Euler and DPM_Solver++ (Table 8), training-prompt sensitivity (Table 13), and global truncation-error comparisons (Figure 4). Component ablations change from FFHQ/Uni_PC to CIFAR10 and FFHQ/DPM_Solver++. Appendix A.2 replaces the CIFAR10 bound experiment with AFHQv2 and FFHQ analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-seed averages and uncertainty throughout its principal FID and ablation tables. v2 removes the explicit pixel-space three-seed statement and replaces most corresponding results with point values, although latent-space three-seed language and AYS-comparison uncertainties remain. Table 13 newly reports averages with uncertainty over five prompt-set runs. These reporting changes do not establish changes in underlying run counts.

E6.justification: Many matched pixel-space scores change: CIFAR10 iPNDM(3M), NFE=4 changes from 12.61 to 9.31, while DPM_Solver++(3M), NFE=7 changes from 3.19 to 5.90 (v1 Table 6; v2 Table 14). v2 adds extensive comparator, text-to-image, ImageNet-64, and pixel-space LSUN results, while removing Euler sweeps and numerous higher-NFE entries. Changed settings and uncertainty reporting limit direct performance conclusions.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 retains the same invertibility and zero-loss assumptions, KL-divergence bound, and Appendix A.1 proof argument. Radius and variance notation receive consistency corrections, but no substantive mathematical result or derivation changes. The new global-error framing is explanatory.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains inexpensive learned discretization without retraining the denoising network. v2 adds explicit comparative contribution claims about training stability, solver/network adaptability, and direct global-error optimization in the introduction and Table 1. This refines the claimed advantages without replacing the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations concerning solver-specific schedules, robustness to training-prompt selection, and performance relative to distillation methods, including inability to generate in one step. Appendix C.1 explicitly acknowledges AYS winning on CIFAR10, and Appendix D.1 discusses uniform discretization winning at 10 NFE. The original differentiability and broader-impact limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link, revises the documented Stable Diffusion teacher configuration, and identifies the 1.5-million-step ImageNet-64 checkpoint and InstaFlow teacher setting. Most optimizer, learning-rate, training-phase, initialization, and rematerialization details are retained. The PDFs establish the new access information, not the repository's actual contents.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially refocused on schedule optimization, adding GITS, DMN, iDDPM, and InstaFlow references and dropping several earlier solver/search references. Table 1 and Appendix C develop new comparisons concerning global versus local error, upper-bound objectives, optimization stability, and solver/network dependence, substantially expanding LD3's positioning.

P1.justification: The introduction, related work, method motivation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves before the background, distillation terminology is reframed around global truncation error, numbered experimental subsections become paragraph headings, and the former additional-results appendix is reorganized into Appendices C and D.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening montage and principal FID plots with a substantially different table-focused presentation. It adds comparison-property, text-to-image, transfer, and benchmark tables plus a global-error plot, redraws the empirical-bound figure, and replaces the Stable Diffusion example galleries. Several existing schematics, training plots, and sample grids are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The added modern baselines, quantitative text-to-image tests, and diagnostic analyses address important gaps in v1. However, v2 removes uncertainty from most central results and introduces reporting conflicts: Table 18 assigns conventional ImageNet baseline values to different solver groups than Table 4, and Appendix B.1 retains a 10-NFE teacher description conflicting with B.1.3. These problems weaken the auditability of key comparisons, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
